allowed_use: Bounded calibration inputs after point, scope, and time-basis review only. This artifact is not a frozen EnergyPlus schedule or calibration target.

source_release.acquisition_transport: Zenodo mirror staged as a manual release directory; mirror URL/version still requires reconciliation in the acquisition manifest

primary_source_schedule_facts.fact: The published load-shape discussion says MEL demand starts rising around 07:00, lighting around 05:00, and summer HVAC remains high during building operating hours until about 18:00.
primary_source_schedule_facts.use: Cross-check only; these statements do not define an annual schedule.

primary_source_schedule_facts.fact: The later operator schedule was weekday occupied 05:00-22:00 all year; RTUs were otherwise off except for setback calls.
primary_source_schedule_facts.use: Later-period sensitivity hypothesis only; not evidence that 2018-2020 used the same enable schedule.

analysis_method.timestamp_parsing: Each CSV used its observed exact format; no shared timezone was assigned or converted.
analysis_method.weekday_definition: Monday-Friday by each file's parsed raw-naive date; holidays were not removed.
analysis_method.weekend_definition: Saturday-Sunday by each file's parsed raw-naive date.
analysis_method.aggregation: For each signal, arithmetic mean of observed native samples within source-clock date/hour, followed by the median across dates for each day type and hour.
analysis_method.missing_policy: No new interpolation, forward fill, backward fill, timezone fill, or gap synthesis. Null values were dropped per signal. Every occurrence of an ambiguous duplicate timestamp was excluded from profile calculations.
analysis_method.upstream_curation_warning: The published clean release was already gap-filled upstream using linear, KNN, and matrix-factorization methods. This analysis adds no imputation, but cannot reconstruct which individual clean values were imputed from the CSV alone.
analysis_method.normalization: Lighting and MEL schedules are divided by the 2018 weekday maximum hourly median and retain standby load. Camera occupancy uses its observed zero-based fraction. Wi-Fi timing fraction subtracts its weekday minimum background before scaling; Wi-Fi remains a device proxy, not a people fraction. Fan speed is divided by 100, not rescaled to its daily peak.
analysis_method.active_hour_diagnostic: An hour is active when the weekday hourly median is at least minimum plus 20 percent of the minimum-to-maximum range. This diagnostic is evaluated in source-clock hours and does not authorize a timezone conversion.

occ.csv.dst_test: 2018-11-04 contains 1,440 unique one-minute records and one copy of every source-clock hour; fall-back semantics are not represented as civil-time repeated timestamps.
occ.csv.time_basis_status: UNRESOLVED; profile timing and zero-lag correlation with ele.csv support the same clock family as ele.csv, not Wi-Fi.

wifi.csv.dst_test: 2020-03-08 contains 288 five-minute records including hour 02, while 2020-11-01 contains 300 rows, a repeated hour 01, and 12 duplicate timestamps. DST treatment is therefore source-specific and cannot be inferred as a single clean convention.
wifi.csv.time_basis_status: UNRESOLVED; 2018 Wi-Fi aligns to occupancy/MEL shape only after an approximately 6-7 hour shift.

rtu_fan_spd.csv.dst_test: Spring transition days retain 1,440 source-clock minutes. Fall dates vary because of missing/15-minute blocks rather than a consistent repeated-hour convention.
quality_flags: The four-RTU median feedback is about 73-76 percent at every 2018 source-clock hour and is similar on weekends.
Negative supply-fan feedback values remain in 2019/early-2020 despite the clean-release label.
This point cannot establish an on/off availability schedule until feedback scaling, off-state encoding, and upstream imputation are reviewed.

ele.csv.dst_test: All six 2018-2020 US DST transition dates contain 96 unique quarter-hour records and every source-clock hour. The file does not encode civil-time skipped/repeated hours.
ele.csv.time_basis_status: UNRESOLVED; profile timing and zero-lag correlation with occ.csv place them in the same clock family.

cross_file_time_tests.method: Spearman and Pearson correlation of separately aggregated observed hourly values over integer shifts from -12 to +12 hours; no interpolation.

results.near_tie: -7 hours also gave Spearman 0.7757 and Pearson 0.8667

cross_file_time_tests.interpretation: A candidate hypothesis is that occ.csv and ele.csv are UTC-naive while Wi-Fi is local-naive. This is not proven and no timezone conversion is authorized until metadata and BAS alignment resolve it.

camera_south_office_sum.unit: camera-derived people count for south halves only
camera_south_office_sum.scope_warning: Not a whole-office occupant count; do not use count amplitude without a reviewed spatial expansion.

wifi_south_office_sum.scope_warning: Large night/weekend device background and short summer-only 2018 coverage make amplitude unsuitable as a people schedule.

rtu_common_supply_fan_feedback.availability_interpretation: UNRESOLVED; nonzero feedback at all hours does not prove intentional 24-hour enablement.

lighting_south_kw.scope_warning: South-wing lighting only; north-wing lighting is absent.

regime_contrasts.basis: Median weekday daily mean in each source file's naive clock; no new imputation.
regime_contrasts.interpretation: 2020 lighting and MEL profiles are pandemic/control-regime evidence, not normal-office schedule priors. Fan feedback did not fall with occupancy and must not be used as an occupancy proxy.

bounded_calibration_priors.time_basis_gate: BLOCKED until source-clock semantics are frozen per file and transformed to the EnergyPlus calendar without unexplained phase shift.

people_schedule.amplitude_rule: Do not convert south-wing camera counts or Wi-Fi devices to whole-office people without a reviewed spatial/count model.

lighting_schedule_south.scope_rule: South-wing only; north lighting remains unresolved.

hypotheses.warning: Observed feedback is nonzero but may not encode enable state.
Direct later-period source fact; not evidence for 2018-2020. Unoccupied setback calls still occur.

rtu_availability.selection_rule: Do not continuously optimize between these hypotheses. Resolve historical enable/off-state semantics from BAS points or carry both as explicitly named sensitivity cases before the calibration campaign.

blocking_limitations: No source CSV contains an explicit timezone or UTC offset.
Cross-file lag and DST tests show that one global timezone assumption is unsafe.
The clean release already contains substantial upstream imputation, especially electricity; this analysis adds none but cannot identify every imputed cell.
Camera occupancy covers only south halves and only 2018-05-22 through 2019-02-21.
2018 Wi-Fi covers only 51 summer days; the next segment begins in February 2020 and crosses the pandemic.
Fan feedback has mixed cadence, remaining negative values outside 2018, and no clear off-state.
Lighting is south-wing only; no north lighting schedule can be inferred as measured.
2020 pandemic, wildfire, RBC additions, and MPC periods are separate regimes and cannot define a normal-office prior.
